title: Cast out, but covered
teaser: Day 7 of Bible 365 — God seeks Adam first, then clothes him. Mercy precedes the expulsion.
framework: Genesis 3:8-9, 21 — God still clothes us. The first sacrifice in Scripture covers shame.

panels.heading: OPENING — A QUIET WALK
panels.content:
It is the seventh day. The week's reading slows here.

Genesis 3 ends in the cool of an evening. Two people are hiding in a garden they were given. The fruit has been eaten. Shame has shown up for the first time. And then, in the breeze of the day, footsteps.

Not the footsteps of judgment. The footsteps of God.

Sit with that for a moment before you read further. The first thing the Lord does after the fall is walk.

panels.heading: TEACHING — WHERE ARE YOU
panels.content:
Genesis 3:8-9 (BSB):

**"Then the man and his wife heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden. So the LORD God called out to the man, 'Where are you?'"**

The question is not for information. God knows where Adam is. The question is for Adam.

Notice the order. Before judgment, a walk. Before sentencing, a search. Before the garments of skin, a voice that comes looking. Mercy moves first.

The rabbis read the Hebrew here as God walking already in the cool of the day, as if this were habit, as if Adam had walked with God in the evenings before and was missing tonight. The first thing the fall steals is the evening walk. The first thing God does is take the walk anyway, and call.

Matthew Henry put it this way: God came not as a judge with a warrant, but as a friend looking for one who had wandered.

panels.heading: CENTER — GARMENTS OF SKIN
panels.content:
Then comes verse 21:

**"And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them."**

The Hebrew is **כֻּתֳּנוֹת עוֹר**, *kuttonot or*, tunics of skin. Adam and Eve had sewn fig leaves. God replaces the leaves with something only a death can give. An animal dies in the garden so that two who hid can be covered. This is the first sacrifice in Scripture, and God Himself performs it.

The leaves were what shame could make. The skins were what only God could make. One came from creature; the other came at the cost of one.

panels.heading: RESPONSE — STAY HERE
panels.content:
There is no to-do list today.

This is the sabbath. Stop reading after this panel. Set the phone face down. Sit for five minutes (actual minutes) and let one phrase from above hold you.

Maybe it is *Where are you*. Maybe it is *He clothed them*. Maybe it is the picture of a God who walks in the cool of the evening looking for the ones who hid.

You do not have to do anything with it. Just let it sit on you, the way the skins sat on Adam.

panels.heading: CLOSING — THE LONG ECHO
panels.content:
What began with skins ends with a robe.

Isaiah will sing of being clothed with garments of salvation, wrapped in a robe of righteousness (Isaiah 61:10). Paul will tell the Galatians that all who were baptized into Christ have **put on Christ** (Galatians 3:27). John will see a great multitude in robes washed white in the blood of the Lamb (Revelation 7:14).

The story of Scripture is, in part, a story of clothing. The garden gave the first thread.

panels.heading: A PRAYER FOR THE EVENING
panels.content:
Lord,

Thank You for walking still.
Thank You that the first word after the fall was a question, not a sentence.
Thank You for the skins. Thank You for the robe.

Where I have hidden today, find me.
Where I have sewn fig leaves, undress me gently.
Clothe me again in what only You can give.

Let this be enough for tonight.

Amen.

sources: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible, Vol. 1 (Genesis), on Genesis 3:8-9 — paraphrased.
